{{Short description|Japanese physicist (1930–2021)}}
{{Nihongo|'''Kyozi Kawasaki'''|川崎 恭治|Kawasaki Kyōji|4 August 1930 — 12 November 2021<ref>{{ Cite journal | title = Kyozi Kawasaki | journal = [[Physics Today]] | doi = 10.1063/PT.3.4987 | volume = 75 | issue = 4 | date = April 2022 | page = 60 | last1 = Andelman | first1 = David | last2 = Brand | first2 = Helmut | last3 = Ohta | first3 = Takao | last4 = Onuki | first4 = Akira | bibcode = 2022PhT....75d..60A | s2cid = 247906400 | doi-access = free }}</ref>}} was a Japanese physicist. His research interests include [[chemical physics]] and [[statistical mechanics]]. In 2001, Kawasaki was awarded the [[Boltzmann Medal]] for "his contribution to our understanding of dynamic phenomena in condensed matter systems, in particular the [[mode-coupling theory]] of fluids near criticality, and nonlinear problems, such as critical phenomena in sheared fluids and phase separations".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://iupap.cii.fc.ul.pt/Boltz_Award/BA2001.html |title=The Boltzmann Award |accessdate=2010-07-09 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110810060505/http://iupap.cii.fc.ul.pt/Boltz_Award/BA2001.html |archivedate=2011-08-10 }} IUPAP page, Accessed July 9, 2010</ref>

==Academic background==
Kawasaki was born on 4 August 1930 in [[Ōtsu, Shiga]], Japan. He received his B.Sc. (1953) and M.Sc. (1955) in physics from [[Kyushu University]], followed by his Ph.D. in physics from [[Duke University]] in 1959. He has held a number of appointments in Japan and in the United States since then.<ref>"Kyozi Kawasaki -- biographical sketch", Physica A, '''204''', 800 (1994)</ref>
* JSPS Research Fellow at [[Kyushu University]] (1959–1960) and [[Kyoto University]]
(1960–1962)
* Instructor, [[Nagoya University]], 1962–1963
* Research Associate, [[M.I.T.]], 1963–1966
* Associate Professor, [[Kyushu University]], 1966–1970
* Associate Professor, [[Temple University]], 1970–1972
* Professor, [[Temple University]], 1972–1973
* Professor, Research Institute for Fundamental Physics, [[Kyoto University]],
1973-1976
* Professor, Department of Physics, [[Kyushu University]], 1976–2001
* Professor, Department of Physics, [[Chubu University]], 2001–2007
* Electronics Research Laboratory, [[Fukuoka Institute of Technology]], 2008-

==Recognition==
* [[Nishina Memorial Prize]], 1972<ref>[http://www.nishina-mf.or.jp/NishinaMemorialPrize-E.html Nishina Memorial Prize], Nishina Memorial Foundation. Accessed July 8, 2010</ref>
* [[Humboldt Prize]], 1992
* [[Boltzmann Medal]], 2001
* Ulam Scholar, 2001-02<ref>[http://cnls.lanl.gov/External/Ulam.php List of Los Alamos Ulam Scholars, Accessed February 9, 2011]</ref>
